methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $150M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Distalmotion is a Series G robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $150M+ to date. The relevant comp universe spans 10 peers in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms such as Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, peer-median valuation was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable framework, using the $150M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical of Series G advancement. This produces an implied valuation of $188M. This method acknowledges that at Series G, capital raised serves as a reasonable anchor, though it does not capture market-specific growth trajectories or unit economics absent from the data set.

The triangulated valuation range is $159M (low) to $216M (high), with a median point of $188M. This relatively tight band reflects reliance on a single methodology and underscores the core limitation: the Robotics & Manufacturing peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or valuation-comparable private companies to apply cross-sectional methods. Key uncertainties include the company's unit economics, revenue scale, and customer concentration relative to the identified peer group. Expanded data on later-stage robotics transactions would strengthen conviction in this range.
